title: Exercise class 6: the Enlightenment, colonization, constitutionalism

6.title: Why the voyages of discovery forced the jurists back to natural law
6.text: The exercise class gives Vitoria a context that is itself the answer. THE VOYAGES OF DISCOVERY OF THE 15TH AND 16TH CENTURIES RAISED LEGAL QUESTIONS FOR WHICH TRADITIONAL LAW HAD NO SOLUTION — to whom do the newly found lands belong, what is the standing of their inhabitants, may war be waged against them. At the same time THE CATHOLIC CHURCH LOST ITS AUTHORITY AS A RESULT OF THE REFORMATION, so NEW SOURCES OF LEGAL KNOWLEDGE had to be found. And because THERE WAS VERY LITTLE POSITIVE LAW ON THE IUS GENTIUM, THE JURISTS REACHED AGAIN AND AGAIN FOR NATURAL LAW — hence 'SPANISH LATE SCHOLASTICISM' and the SCHOOL OF SALAMANCA. That is: natural law did not return out of philosophical taste but BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING ELSE TO HAND. FRANCISCO DE VITORIA (1483–1546) TO SOME EXTENT OVERCAME MEDIEVAL LEGAL THINKING, which had been wholly dominated by Christian natural law; he uses the SCHOLASTIC METHOD and proceeds from ARISTOTLE, and his teaching STANDS AGAINST THE SO-CALLED 'IDEOLOGY OF THE CONQUISTADORS'. AND NOW THE UNCOMFORTABLE POINT THE EXERCISE DOES NOT CONCEAL: THE PROPONENTS OF THE CONQUISTADOR IDEOLOGY ALSO INVOKED ARISTOTLE IN SUBJUGATING THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES — namely his thesis that THERE ARE PEOPLE WHO ARE SLAVES BY NATURE AND AGAINST WHOM WAR IS BY NATURE JUSTIFIED. The same author thus served both sides of the dispute.

cards.q: Why did the jurists return to natural law after the voyages of discovery?
cards.a: Because THE VOYAGES RAISED QUESTIONS FOR WHICH TRADITIONAL LAW HAD NO SOLUTION, THE CATHOLIC CHURCH LOST ITS AUTHORITY THROUGH THE REFORMATION, and THERE WAS VERY LITTLE POSITIVE LAW ON THE IUS GENTIUM. Natural law therefore returned not out of philosophical taste but BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING ELSE TO HAND — hence SPANISH LATE SCHOLASTICISM and the SCHOOL OF SALAMANCA.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: How did Aristotle serve both sides of the dispute over conquest?
cards.a: VITORIA proceeds from him by the scholastic method and sets his teaching AGAINST THE 'IDEOLOGY OF THE CONQUISTADORS'. BUT THE PROPONENTS OF THAT IDEOLOGY ALSO INVOKED ARISTOTLE IN SUBJUGATING THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES — namely his thesis that THERE ARE PEOPLE WHO ARE SLAVES BY NATURE AND AGAINST WHOM WAR IS BY NATURE JUSTIFIED.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

8.title: The three components out of which international law arose as a discipline
8.text: To the question 'when and in what circumstances did the ius gentium become an independent discipline' the exercise class gives a clear trio worth knowing. THE HISTORICAL BACKGROUND: THE SPANISH ERA (1500–1648), that is, the REFORMATION, the DISCOVERY OF AMERICA, the RELIGIOUS WARS IN EUROPE and the PEACE OF WESTPHALIA. THE THREE POLITICAL-PHILOSOPHICAL COMPONENTS: (a) LATE SPANISH SCHOLASTICISM — FRANCISCO SUÁREZ (1548–1617) with his distinction of the IUS GENTIUM INTER SE (external) and INTRA SE (internal); (b) POLITICAL THEORY — founded by NICCOLÒ MACHIAVELLI (1469–1527) with IL PRINCIPE, according to which IN EXTREME CASES THE INTERESTS OF POWER MUST TAKE PRECEDENCE OVER LAW AND MORALITY, and JEAN BODIN (1530–1596) with the MODERN CONCEPT OF SOVEREIGNTY; (c) LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP INFLUENCED BY HUMANISM — under its influence GROTIUS developed a new view of the ius gentium and of natural law. GROTIUS IS OFTEN REGARDED AS THE 'FATHER OF INTERNATIONAL LAW' precisely because he combined all three currents: the humanist method, secularized natural law and the system of sovereign states.

cards.q: Out of which three components did international law arise as an independent discipline?
cards.a: a) LATE SPANISH SCHOLASTICISM — SUÁREZ with the distinction of the ius gentium INTER SE and INTRA SE. b) POLITICAL THEORY — MACHIAVELLI (Il principe: in extreme cases THE INTERESTS OF POWER MUST TAKE PRECEDENCE OVER LAW AND MORALITY) and BODIN (the modern concept of sovereignty). c) LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP INFLUENCED BY HUMANISM — through which GROTIUS developed his new view.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: Why is Grotius regarded as the 'father of international law'?
cards.a: Because he COMBINED ALL THREE CURRENTS: THE HUMANIST METHOD, SECULARIZED NATURAL LAW and THE SYSTEM OF SOVEREIGN STATES.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

11.title: The papal bulls, Tordesillas and occupation in the ius gentium
11.text: To the legal titles of colonization the exercise class gives exact dates and one conceptual shift that is the heart of the matter. SPANISH EXPANSION FROM THE 16TH CENTURY WAS LEGITIMATED BY THE MISSION OF SPREADING CHRISTIANITY. THE PAPAL BULLS OF DONATION: two series by which POPE NICHOLAS V IN 1454 AND POPE ALEXANDER VI IN 1493 were to grant the Catholic monarchs of Portugal and Spain the exclusive right to explore new lands. THE TREATY OF TORDESILLAS (1494) DIVIDED THE NEWLY DISCOVERED LANDS OUTSIDE EUROPE BETWEEN PORTUGAL AND SPAIN (the Crown of Castile) ALONG A MERIDIAN 370 LEAGUES WEST OF THE CAPE VERDE ISLANDS — the dividing line lay roughly midway between the Cape Verde Islands (already Portuguese) and the islands visited by Columbus (claimed for Castile and León). To this belongs the TREATY OF ZARAGOZA (1529), which divided the Pacific as well. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR LAW: SPANISH EXPANSION LED TO THE SPREAD OF THE LEARNED LAWS (CANON AND ROMAN) TO THE AMERICAS. AND NOW THE CONCEPTUAL SHIFT: IN THE 16TH CENTURY THE IDEA OF ACQUIRING POSSESSION BY OCCUPATION WAS TRANSFERRED INTO THE IUS GENTIUM (VITORIA, ALBERICO GENTILI), WHICH MEANS THAT THE ACQUISITION OF UNOCCUPIED LAND IS LEGITIMATED ON THE BASIS OF NATURAL LAW. Occupation is originally an institution of Roman PRIVATE law concerning the acquisition of a thing belonging to no one — and it was precisely its transfer to whole countries that turned colonization into a legal transaction.

cards.q: What did the Treaty of Tordesillas provide and which bulls preceded it?
cards.a: IN 1494 IT DIVIDED THE NEWLY DISCOVERED LANDS OUTSIDE EUROPE BETWEEN PORTUGAL AND SPAIN ALONG A MERIDIAN 370 LEAGUES WEST OF THE CAPE VERDE ISLANDS. It was preceded by the PAPAL BULLS OF DONATION — of NICHOLAS V (1454) and ALEXANDER VI (1493); it was supplemented by the TREATY OF ZARAGOZA (1529) for the Pacific.

cards.q: Which conceptual shift turned colonization into a legal transaction?
cards.a: IN THE 16TH CENTURY THE IDEA OF ACQUIRING POSSESSION BY OCCUPATION WAS TRANSFERRED INTO THE IUS GENTIUM (Vitoria, Alberico Gentili) — the acquisition of UNOCCUPIED LAND is legitimated by NATURAL LAW. OCCUPATION is originally an institution of Roman PRIVATE law on acquiring A THING BELONGING TO NO ONE, and its transfer to WHOLE COUNTRIES is what turned colonization into a legal transaction.

12.title: Vattel: occupation fused with sovereignty, and the argument from use
12.text: EMER DE VATTEL (1714–1776) published his main work 'THE LAW OF NATIONS' in 1758. The exercise class describes his contribution to colonization precisely: THE FUSION OF THE IDEA OF OCCUPATION WITH MODERN CONCEPTIONS OF SOVEREIGNTY LED TO THE DOCTRINE OF 'TERRA NULLIUS'. As long as occupation was merely an institution of private law, what was acquired by it was a thing; only in combination with sovereignty does it acquire DOMINION OVER A TERRITORY. IN HIS TREATISE VATTEL ATTEMPTED TO CREATE A LEGAL BASIS FOR THE DIVISION OF THE WORLD INTO COLONIES. By using the CONCEPT OF THE NATION he united the interest of the state (RAISON D'ÉTAT) with the interests of the people and elevated justice into the governing norm of relations between states. His concrete instrument has its own name in German: 'NUTZUNGS- UND KULTIVIERUNGSARGUMENT', the ARGUMENT FROM USE AND CULTIVATION — whoever does not cultivate the land has no full claim to it. And recall how far that argument goes in his text: peoples who do not cultivate fertile land, he writes, 'DESERVE TO BE EXTERMINATED LIKE WILD AND NOXIOUS BEASTS'.

terms.def: Whoever does not cultivate the land has no full claim to it — Vattel's instrument for legitimating colonial seizure.

cards.q: How did the doctrine of terra nullius arise in Vattel?
cards.a: BY THE FUSION OF THE IDEA OF OCCUPATION WITH MODERN CONCEPTIONS OF SOVEREIGNTY. As long as occupation was merely a PRIVATE-LAW institution, what it acquired was A THING; combined with sovereignty it acquires DOMINION OVER A TERRITORY. In his treatise Vattel ATTEMPTED TO CREATE A LEGAL BASIS FOR THE DIVISION OF THE WORLD INTO COLONIES.

cards.q: What is the 'argument from use and cultivation'?
cards.a: Vattel's instrument (NUTZUNGS- UND KULTIVIERUNGSARGUMENT): WHOEVER DOES NOT CULTIVATE THE LAND HAS NO FULL CLAIM TO IT. By using the CONCEPT OF THE NATION he united the INTEREST OF THE STATE with the interests of the people and elevated justice into the governing norm — and in his text he goes as far as saying that such peoples 'DESERVE TO BE EXTERMINATED LIKE WILD AND NOXIOUS BEASTS'.

15.title: Constitutionalism and whom it actually brought in
15.text: To the constitutional movement the exercise class gives two things worth remembering, both of which cut against simplification. (1) 'CONSTITUTIONALISM' IS A PAN-EUROPEAN PHENOMENON WHICH IN CONTINENTAL EUROPE RUNS FROM 1789 — and the exercise calls it the LOGICAL CONTINUATION OF ENLIGHTENED ABSOLUTISM, not its negation. The enlightened ruler already ruled FOR his subjects; the constitution added that they should also rule THROUGH them. (2) THE CONSTITUTIONS PUT AN END TO ABSOLUTE MONARCHY BY LIMITING THE RULER'S POWER AND SECURING THE PARTICIPATION OF THE BOURGEOISIE — AND THE EXERCISE STRESSES THIS EXPRESSLY: NOT OF THE WORKING CLASS. This is the key to understanding the 19th century: the franchise was tied to property and its extension to the workers comes only generations later. THE STATE IS NOT MERELY TO ACT IN THE INTEREST OF ITS SUBJECTS — THE SUBJECTS THEMSELVES ARE TO TAKE PART IN THE AFFAIRS OF STATE. And one further connection: THE TRANSFORMATION FROM A 'COMMUNITY OF SUBJECTS' INTO A 'PEOPLE OF THE STATE' PLAYED A GREAT PART IN THE RISE OF NATIONALISM, AND CONVERSELY NATIONALISM BECAME THE DRIVING FORCE OF CONSTITUTIONALISM. THE RISING BOURGEOISIE BECOMES THE CENTRAL PLAYER DEMANDING THE NEW POLITICAL ORDER.

cards.q: Whom did constitutionalism bring into the affairs of state, and whom not?
cards.a: The constitutions limited the ruler's power and SECURED THE PARTICIPATION OF THE BOURGEOISIE — EXPRESSLY NOT OF THE WORKING CLASS. The franchise was TIED TO PROPERTY and its extension to the workers comes only generations later.

cards.q: How are constitutionalism and nationalism connected?
cards.a: THE TRANSFORMATION FROM A 'COMMUNITY OF SUBJECTS' INTO A 'PEOPLE OF THE STATE' PLAYED A GREAT PART IN THE RISE OF NATIONALISM — AND CONVERSELY NATIONALISM BECAME THE DRIVING FORCE OF CONSTITUTIONALISM. The rising bourgeoisie becomes the central player demanding the new order.

cards.q: Why is constitutionalism the 'logical continuation' of enlightened absolutism?
cards.a: Because THE ENLIGHTENED RULER ALREADY RULED FOR HIS SUBJECTS — the constitution merely added that they should also rule THROUGH THEM. It is therefore not a negation but a further step: the state is not merely to act in the subjects' interest, THE SUBJECTS THEMSELVES ARE TO TAKE PART IN THE AFFAIRS OF STATE.

16.title: Kant, Locke, Montesquieu: three cornerstones of constitutionalism
16.text: THE PHILOSOPHICAL BACKGROUND is the ENLIGHTENMENT and MODERN NATURAL-LAW THINKING, whose key element is REASON — hence the NATURAL RIGHTS OF THE PERSON and the IDEA OF INDIVIDUAL FREEDOM (Kant, Voltaire, Rousseau, Hume). IMMANUEL KANT (1724–1804) formulates it in a sentence worth knowing: 'FREEDOM […] INSOFAR AS IT CAN COEXIST WITH THE FREEDOM OF EVERY OTHER IN ACCORDANCE WITH A UNIVERSAL LAW; IT IS THE ONE SOLE ORIGINAL, INNATE RIGHT BELONGING TO EVERY MAN BY VIRTUE OF HIS HUMANITY.' This is called the UNIVERSAL LAW OF FREEDOM. THE PRECURSOR OF THE ENLIGHTENMENT IN CONTINENTAL EUROPE IS JOHN LOCKE (1632–1704). Closely connected with him is the LIMITATION OF THE RULER'S POWER, WHICH ORIGINATES IN 17TH-CENTURY ENGLAND — the BILL OF RIGHTS (1689), by which parliament obtained the RIGHT TO ENACT STATUTES, and this, according to the exercise, is the BEGINNING OF CONSTITUTIONALISM. LOCKE CHANGED HOBBES'S THEORY OF THE SOCIAL CONTRACT: THE SOVEREIGN IS INSTITUTED FOR THE GOOD OF THE SUBJECT, and therefore THE PEOPLE — note, THE PEOPLE, NOT THE INDIVIDUAL — HAVE A RIGHT OF RESISTANCE. He also came up with the IDEA OF THE SEPARATION OF POWERS to secure individual freedom, wishing to separate the LEGISLATIVE FROM THE EXECUTIVE POWER. MONTESQUIEU LATER DISTINGUISHED THREE POWERS and added a qualification that is often forgotten: ALTHOUGH THEY HAD TO BE SEPARATED, EACH OF THEM HAD TO BE ABLE TO ACT ON THE OTHERS IN SOME WAY IN ORDER TO PREVENT THEIR ABUSE. And his threshold: IF EVEN TWO OF THOSE POWERS ARE CONCENTRATED IN ONE HAND, THERE IS NO FREEDOM.

cards.a: 'FREEDOM INSOFAR AS IT CAN COEXIST WITH THE FREEDOM OF EVERY OTHER IN ACCORDANCE WITH A UNIVERSAL LAW; IT IS THE ONE SOLE ORIGINAL, INNATE RIGHT BELONGING TO EVERY MAN BY VIRTUE OF HIS HUMANITY.' This is called the UNIVERSAL LAW OF FREEDOM.

cards.q: To whom does the right of resistance belong according to Locke, and what did he want to separate?
cards.a: TO THE PEOPLE — note, THE PEOPLE, NOT THE INDIVIDUAL. The sovereign is instituted FOR THE GOOD OF THE SUBJECT, and if he abuses his power the people have a right of resistance. Locke wanted to separate the LEGISLATIVE FROM THE EXECUTIVE POWER in order to secure individual freedom.

cards.q: What qualification did Montesquieu add to the separation of powers, and what threshold did he set?
cards.a: That ALTHOUGH THE POWERS MUST BE SEPARATED, EACH MUST BE ABLE TO ACT ON THE OTHERS IN SOME WAY in order to prevent their abuse — it is therefore not merely separation but mutual checking. And the threshold: IF EVEN TWO OF THOSE POWERS ARE CONCENTRATED IN ONE HAND, THERE IS NO FREEDOM.

18.title: The Declaration of 1789: the content of Arts 1 and 2 and its predecessors
18.text: Alongside Art. 16 the exercise class quotes the first two articles as well, and they are worth knowing, because the whole structure follows from them. ART. 1: 'MEN ARE BORN AND REMAIN FREE AND EQUAL IN RIGHTS. SOCIAL DISTINCTIONS MAY BE FOUNDED ONLY UPON CONSIDERATIONS OF THE COMMON GOOD.' Note that equality is not absolute: distinctions MAY exist, but ONLY FOR REASONS OF THE COMMON GOOD, not by birth. ART. 2: 'THE AIM OF EVERY POLITICAL ASSOCIATION IS THE PRESERVATION OF THE NATURAL AND IMPRESCRIPTIBLE RIGHTS OF MAN. THESE RIGHTS ARE LIBERTY, PROPERTY, SECURITY AND RESISTANCE TO OPPRESSION.' Four rights — and note at once that RESISTANCE TO OPPRESSION IS AMONG THEM, that is, that the right of resistance is placed there as an ordinary natural right, not as a last-resort exception. THE ORIGIN: THE DECLARATION IS INSPIRED BY THE AMERICAN DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE OF 1776 AND BY THE SPIRIT OF THE ENLIGHTENMENT and is a PRODUCT OF THE FRENCH REVOLUTION OF 1789; its PREDECESSOR is the VIRGINIA BILL OF RIGHTS, the FIRST 'CATALOGUE' OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS. It consists of a PREAMBLE AND 17 ARTICLES and sets out 'NATURAL AND INVIOLABLE' RIGHTS. The exercise sums it up as the BEGINNING OF A NEW POLITICAL ERA.

cards.q: What does Art. 1 of the Declaration say and how is equality conceived there?
cards.a: 'MEN ARE BORN AND REMAIN FREE AND EQUAL IN RIGHTS. SOCIAL DISTINCTIONS MAY BE FOUNDED ONLY UPON CONSIDERATIONS OF THE COMMON GOOD.' Equality is therefore NOT ABSOLUTE: distinctions MAY exist, but ONLY FOR REASONS OF THE COMMON GOOD, not by birth.

cards.q: Which four rights does Art. 2 of the Declaration name, and what is remarkable about the list?
cards.a: LIBERTY, PROPERTY, SECURITY AND RESISTANCE TO OPPRESSION — the aim of every political association is their preservation. What is remarkable is that RESISTANCE TO OPPRESSION IS AMONG THEM, that is, that the right of resistance is placed there as an ORDINARY NATURAL RIGHT, not as a last-resort exception.
